questions.question:
Lactic acid bacteria (LAB), particularly Lactobacillus, are widely used in the preparation of curd and other fermented milk products. During fermentation, these bacteria convert lactose present in milk into lactic acid. The accumulation of lactic acid lowers the pH, leading to coagulation of milk proteins such as casein. In addition to improving texture and taste, LAB also enhance the nutritional quality of curd by increasing vitamin B12 content and inhibiting the growth of harmful microbes in the digestive tract.
Statements:
Statement-1 :- During curd formation, lactic acid bacteria convert lactose into lactic acid, which lowers the pH of milk, causes coagulation of casein proteins, improves digestibility, enhances vitamin B12 content, and suppresses the growth of pathogenic microorganisms in the gut.
Statement-2 :- The sour taste and thick consistency of curd are primarily due to the production of carbon dioxide by lactic acid bacteria during aerobic respiration inside milk.
Options:
options: Both statement-1 and statement-2 are correct
Both statement-1 and statement-2 are incorrect
Statement-1 is correct but statement-2 is incorrect
Statement-1 is incorrect but statement-2 is correct
